items.summary_1line: Every multimodal-LLM multiple-choice benchmark ends with a scoring rule that converts a model's response, often free-form text rather than a clean option letter, into a right/wrong verdict, buried in its code. items.editor_note: Audits the scoring rules of multimodal multiple-choice benchmarks, which can score identical outputs differently.

items.title: Same Model, Different Harness: CUGA, Hermes, and Deep Agents — When to Pick CUGA?
items.summary_1line: Same Model, Different Harness: CUGA, Hermes, and Deep Agents — When to Pick CUGA?
items.editor_note: IBM Research frames CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents as harnesses around one model and asks when to choose CUGA.

editorial.tldr: Most of this thread shares a "Same X, Different Y" title pattern, not one event. Three arXiv papers (Oct 22-26) cover chemistry identifier binding, credit assignment for agentic RL and news framing; a Nov 1 post then reported a 17-point gap between agents using one model.
editorial.whats_new: On Nov 3, an IBM Research Hugging Face post compared CUGA, Hermes and Deep Agents on the same model, a day after an arXiv audit showed multimodal benchmark graders can change scores on identical outputs.
editorial.why_it_matters: Harness posts and the grader audit point the same way: scores depend on the agent harness and the scoring rule as much as the model, so evaluate the full stack, including how answers are graded.
editorial.take_for_builders: Hold the model fixed and vary the harness in your own eval on your MCP servers, and pin and review your scoring rule; treat the 17-point figure and IBM's CUGA comparison as vendor or blog results until reproduced.

status.detail: Title-match papers are coincidental; the Nov 1 and Nov 3 posts plus the Nov 2 grader audit form the real thread on non-model variance in evals.
